title: Dry Peanut Chutney
name: Dry Peanut Chutney (Shengdana Pudi)
subtitle: A ground peanut condiment with chana dal and sesame — mild enough for the whole family.
protein: ~3g protein per 2 tbsp serving — from peanuts, chana dal & sesame

method.title: Roast peanuts (Ninja Crispi) and sesame
items: Spread {@peanuts} in the Crispi basket in a single layer — you'll likely need 2 batches of {1½ cups} each to avoid steaming
Set to 330°F, 6 min — the Crispi's lowest usable setting; shake the basket at the 3-minute mark
Check at 5 min: fragrant, skins loosening and crackled; since 330°F runs hot for this, add only 1 min at a time from here
Spread on a plate and cool completely, at least 15 min — they crisp further as they cool
Rub between palms to loosen skins; sieve or blow away (a little remaining skin is fine)
Meanwhile, in a dry pan on low, stir {@sesame} constantly 60–90 sec — they pop and jump; keep a lid nearby
Remove the moment they turn lightly golden and smell toasty — they burn in seconds; cool on a separate plate

method.title: Temper the spices
items: Heat {@oil} in a small pan over medium-low
Add {@curry-leaves}; fry 20–30 sec until crisp; remove and set aside
In the same pan on low, add {@chilies} and {@cumin}; roast, stirring, 60–90 sec until cumin is golden — do not blacken
Add {@coconut} (or {2½ tbsp} if thawed frozen) and {@tamarind}; toss 30 sec until coconut is lightly golden
Return the fried leaves to the pan; transfer everything to a plate and cool completely

method.title: Grind — spice base first, then peanuts
items: Add the cooled chili-cumin-coconut-tamarind-curry leaf mixture to a grinder
Add {@chana} and the toasted {@sesame} — these must be ground fine now, not pulsed later with the peanuts
Add {@hing} and {@salt}; grind to a fine powder, 25–35 sec
Add the roasted, cooled {@peanuts}
Pulse only — 3–4 short bursts of 2–3 sec each — until coarse and sandy, not paste
Taste and adjust salt

method.label: Toddler notes
items: This whole batch is already toddler-mild — the 12 Kashmiri chilies give color, not real heat
For more adult heat, add chili flakes separately at serving time rather than into the batch
Serve her portion mixed with a few drops of ghee, or stirred into warm dal-rice for easier eating
Great sprinkled on her soft roti with ghee, or mixed into yogurt rice

method.title: Cool, store, label
items: Spread the finished chutney on a wide plate; rest uncovered 20 min to drive off residual moisture
Transfer to a clean, dry, airtight glass jar and label it with the date made
Store at room temperature 3–4 weeks, or refrigerate to extend to 6–8 weeks — if frozen coconut was used, drop to 2–3 weeks and refrigerate after the first week
Always use a dry spoon — a single drop of moisture shortens shelf life fast

method.label: Tip
method.text: Grind the spice base to a fine powder before the peanuts ever go in, then only pulse the peanuts in short bursts — their oil releases fast and a few seconds too long turns the whole batch into peanut butter. If using frozen coconut, dry it on the stovetop first, not in the Crispi (it browns the dry bits before the wet ones catch up). Great over hot rice with ghee, mixed into yogurt rice, or stuffed into a roti roll.
